result:
The disk filled up and took the database, then the api, with it: the api exited at 03:14:06 and was still down when the log ends at 05:29:57.

The cause was the `report-export` job. Starting at 03:05:00 it wrote 40 files of 512 MB each (about 20 GB) to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` in under eight minutes, on the same volume as the database. Disk went from 91% at 03:09:03 to 99% at 03:13:30, and then:

```
2026-03-09T03:14:00 ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device
2026-03-09T03:14:03 ERROR api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool
2026-03-09T03:14:06 FATAL api: exiting (status 1)
```

From 03:16:00 the proxy logs `upstream api refused connection` every two minutes through 05:28:00, and nothing in the log shows the api restarting.

The `cache: slow command` warnings are unrelated: they run every five minutes or so from 02:00:00, before and after the crash, at the same 100–149 ms.

To recover, free space in `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` and restart the api. To stop a repeat, move the exports to a different volume from the database or cap the job's output. Nothing in this repo defines `report-export`, so I could not check why it wrote that much.

The log is dated 2026-03-09, not last night (today is 2026-10-04), so if the outage you mean just happened, this file may be a stale sample rather than the record of it.
